content: Tokophobia, also known as the fear of childbirth, is classified as a specific phobia. It is also referred to by terms such as tocophobia and parturiphobia. In the year 2000, an article published in the British Journal of Psychiatry (2000, 176: 83-85) identified the fear of childbirth as a psychological disorder. Prior to this, it had received minimal recognition as such. The term tokophobia was introduced in this context, derived from the Greek words tokos (childbirth) and phobos (fear). As with other phobias, the fear of childbirth can present with a variety of symptoms. These may include nightmares, difficulty concentrating on work or family activities, panic attacks, and psychosomatic complaints. In many cases, this fear leads women to request an elective cesarean section. The fear of labor pain is often closely linked to a general fear of pain. Additionally, a history of complicated childbirth or inadequate pain management during a previous delivery can contribute to the development of this phobia. There is ongoing debate within the obstetric and psychiatric communities regarding a woman’s right to choose her mode of delivery. This includes the right to request a cesarean section versus the emphasis on providing methods to help women overcome their fear of vaginal childbirth. Preliminary studies conducted in Sweden and Finland have shown that treatment during pregnancy can be effective. In these studies, more than half of the women who initially requested cesarean sections withdrew their requests after receiving support to discuss their anxiety and fear. Furthermore, vaginal deliveries following such treatment were successful. Tokophobia is a distressing psychological condition that may be overlooked by medical professionals. In addition to being a specific phobia or anxiety disorder, tokophobia can also be associated with depression and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Recognizing tokophobia and fostering close collaboration with obstetricians or other medical specialists can help reduce its severity and ensure effective treatment. Tokophobia can be categorized into two types: primary and secondary. Primary tokophobia refers to a fear of childbirth that predates pregnancy and may begin during adolescence. Secondary tokophobia arises from a previous negative experience, such as a traumatic birth, inadequate obstetric care, postpartum depression, or other distressing events. Both primary and secondary tokophobia can be managed with the assistance of trained medical professionals or psychologists.
